_comment: Consumer access for the Air Monitoring data product.
Applied by the CENTRAL pipeline (Automation_Assign_Consumer_Access) in
da-mdp-automation-deployments — there is deliberately no pipeline here,
because applying this file needs an account-admin identity that data-product
repos must not be able to drive.
Environments: acc and prd only. Consumer groups exist to use apps, and apps are
consumed in acceptance and production; dev/test access belongs to the engineers
through their SEC.RBAC.* groups.
WHY THESE GRANTS MATTER FOR THIS APP
The air-monitoring app runs its SQL as the VISITOR, not as its service principal:
resources/apps/air_monitoring_app.yml declares user_api_scopes: [sql], and
src/utils/db_utils.py opens the connection with the forwarded x-forwarded-access-token.
It refuses to fall back to the service principal, so a visitor who is missing a
grant below gets a permission error rather than silently borrowing the SP's
access. That is what makes these grants load-bearing instead of decorative.
Volume uploads also run as the visitor (upload_file_to_volume uses the forwarded
token), so WRITE_VOLUME is equally load-bearing.
HOW A GRANT WORKS
tier       picks the GROUP.  READ -> AUTOMATION.AIR_MONITORING.CONSUMER.READ
WRITE -> AUTOMATION.AIR_MONITORING.CONSUMER.WRITE
The tier name carries no privilege meaning - it is only the group
suffix.
privileges are real Databricks privileges, exactly as in GRANT ... ON ...
Nothing is added or implied.
Allowed per object (an allow-list - no route to ALL_PRIVILEGES, MANAGE,
CREATE_*, APPLY_TAG or ownership):
catalog  USE_CATALOG, USE_SCHEMA, SELECT
schema   USE_SCHEMA, SELECT, MODIFY
table    SELECT, MODIFY
volume   READ_VOLUME, WRITE_VOLUME
catalog is the BASE name: the pipeline appends _a / _p, so one file serves both
environments. An environment-suffixed catalog is rejected.
The WRITE tier grants MODIFY per table rather than on the schema, so a consumer
can write the app's own tables and nothing else that later lands in the schema.
It relies on its members also being in READ for USE_CATALOG and USE_SCHEMA -
validation warns about exactly that, by design.
Tables the app writes as the visitor are taken from src/utils/db_utils.py.
setup_tables.py is run by the setup job as the service principal, not through
the app, so CREATE TABLE operations do not need a consumer grant.
warehouse: true gives this data product its own warehouse, created and owned by
the pipeline (aut-airmonitoring-consumer-sqlwh-a / -p). Note the bundle
ALSO creates a warehouse and binds it to the app; this pipeline never touches a
warehouse it did not create, so CAN_USE on that one belongs in the bundle.
Members: all @etexgroup.com users listed in automation_d.bronze.air_monitoring_sites.allowed_users
Excluded: @pladur.com addresses (not allowed by guardrails) and users not in the Databricks account.
